source.title: LoDAdaC: a unified local training-based decentralized framework with adaptive gradients and compressed communication
source.authors: Wei Liu; Anweshit Panda; Ujwal Pandey; Haven Cook; George M. Slota; Nai-Gang Wang; Jiewei Chen; Yang-Yang Xu

record.tranche_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD and reports held-out performance: similar test accuracy on CIFAR-10 and significantly worse validation loss for non-adaptive methods on the language-model benchmark.
record.gate_note: The study reports optimizer comparisons bearing on V4. Its figures also show training and held-out metrics, but it does not give exact values for these comparisons in the text. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own adaptive-versus-non-adaptive optimizer comparisons on held-out image and language data in a new decentralized setting with local updates and compressed communication. These bear on V4, although the experiment does not reproduce its original tuning protocol.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Section 4.1 but incompletely represents the paper's conclusion. The authors' main conclusion is that LoDAdaC combines local adaptive updates and compressed communication with convergence guarantees and substantial communication savings while largely preserving accuracy. They report similar CIFAR-10 accuracy for SQuARM-SGD, worse GPT validation loss for both non-adaptive baselines, and generally strong AdaGrad and Adam performance. They acknowledge bounded-gradient assumptions and the small language-model benchmark.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates adaptive and momentum-SGD methods within a decentralized framework that combines multiple local updates and compressed communication; the comparisons use different datasets, training setups, and metrics from the claim's optimizer studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and task affect the comparison: SQuARM-SGD has similar test accuracy on CIFAR-10, while the non-adaptive methods have significantly worse validation loss on tiny-shakespeare.
record.problems: The optimizer comparison is a representative selection from a larger parameter study. The text gives qualitative comparisons without exact metric values or uncertainty estimates. The authors note that language-model experiments are limited to a small-scale transformer benchmark.
record.rows_left_out: No other optimizer-comparison outcomes were stated in prose as separately attributable results for the held-out-performance comparison. Additional plots and appendix comparisons are not assigned exact values from figures.

untested.parts: Natural-label versus fixed-random-label fitting and held-out performance.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

A controlled comparison using the original learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning protocol; broader tuning as an intervention; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; and the specifically word-level language-model exception. Learning rates are reported and SQuARM-SGD's rates were tuned, but the tuning budget and schedule search are not established.
Batch-size variation under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to large batches. Changing local updates between communications does not change minibatch size.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: CDProxSGT reaches lower CIFAR-10 test accuracy than the adaptive methods within the given epoch budget and converges substantially more slowly. Add its own comparison row; do not attribute this result to SQuARM-SGD.
CDProxSGT also has worse GPT validation loss than adaptive methods: the prose explicitly attributes the outcome to both non-adaptive methods. Add a separate row for this algorithm.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source for V4. Appendix optimizer comparisons are already declared under rows_left_out, so they are not listed as newly missing. Exact endpoint metrics cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. Held-out performance at finite training budgets does not isolate generalization differences at matched training loss; slower optimization can contribute to the observed rankings.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests adaptive methods against momentum SGD in decentralized training, not the broader optimizer and benchmark comparisons in the version. It does not report controlled tuning of learning rates and decay schedules, broader tuning, Adam with decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language-model results.
